📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The Stafford Building Society, a UK mutual lender, has deployed MV Shield, the financial crime compliance platform from Mutual Vision that runs on Napier AI technology.

The move brings the Society’s screening, monitoring and case management into a single system.

The rollout moves customer screening, transaction monitoring, customer risk assessment and know-your-customer (KYC) checks onto one unified platform.

Since the launch, initial signs show a drop in false positives, a lighter manual workload and quicker resolution of cases. Each decision is logged in a complete audit trail, which helps the Society prepare for audits and engage with regulators.

The Society chose MV Shield largely because it was built with mutuals in mind. It pairs Napier AI’s detection capabilities, which align with Financial Conduct Authority (FCA) expectations, with Mutual Vision’s experience of working with building societies for more than 25 years, along with locally based support.

Industry observers note that because screening, monitoring and case management sit together in a no-code environment, staff can assess alerts from one page and change rules and thresholds without outside help. They can also trial adjustments in a Sandbox before putting them into production, so they no longer need to raise tickets with the vendor.

MV Shield forms part of Mutual Vision’s updated technology offering for the mutual sector. It was created for the small compliance teams common at smaller societies. It gives them the kind of detection tools normally used by much larger organisations, in a format they can set up, test and manage on their own.

The Stafford Building Society CRO & MLRO Michelle Pledger said, “We are a small team with the same risk exposure as a much bigger one. What sold us was control: screening, monitoring and workflow in one platform, and the ability to change rules and test them ourselves, the same day a risk emerges.”.

It has been revealed that napier AI CEO Greg Watson remarked, “Money laundering cost the UK economy £156.7bn ($206bn) last year and continues to rise, as found by the Napier AI / AML Index 26-27. That means the scale of the challenge of financial crime compliance teams is growing too.

“We are delighted to partner with Mutual Vision to bring best-in-class AML solutions to mutuals, with embedded AI that helps small teams tackle financial crime efficiently without compromising on compliance.”.

CSSF AI questionnaire: what fund managers need to know

📅 25 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (590 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Fintech

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Luxembourg’s investment fund managers have until the end of the year to show the regulator exactly how they use artificial intelligence, and a single answer could determine how much scrutiny follows.
  • According to Zeidler Group, the latest joint survey from the Commission de Surveillance du Secteur Financier (CSSF) and the Banque centrale du Luxembourg (BCL) deserves far more attention than its statistical label suggests.
  • Debuted on 17 November 2026, the questionnaire must be submitted via eDesk by 31 December 2026.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Luxembourg’s investment fund managers have until the end of the year to show the regulator exactly how they use artificial intelligence, and a single answer could determine how much scrutiny follows.

According to Zeidler Group, the latest joint survey from the Commission de Surveillance du Secteur Financier (CSSF) and the Banque centrale du Luxembourg (BCL) deserves far more attention than its statistical label suggests.

Debuted on 17 November 2026, the questionnaire must be submitted via eDesk by 31 December 2026. Authorised investment fund managers are among the addressees, alongside banks, investment firms, payment and e-money institutions, specialised and support PFS, crypto-asset service providers and Luxembourg branches.

Zeidler Group notes that while the exercise is framed as a survey, it hands the CSSF a detailed view of each manager’s AI usage, governance arrangements and dependence on third-party providers.

Recent findings suggest that this is the third AI survey run jointly by the two authorities. The first, held between October 2021 and January 2022, covered only credit, payment and e-money institutions. Fund managers were brought in for the second round in mid-2024, and the findings, published in May 2025, explain the regulator’s interest.

Investment fund managers made up the largest respondent group, at 261 of 461 participants. Roughly half were already using AI or planned to within a year, and they were the only category where most machine learning use cases (57%) depended on third-party vendor solutions. Across all respondents, only 43% had a formally approved AI policy.

In a recent development, on eDesk, the procedure sits under “Investment funds and vehicles / Investment fund managers”. Zeidler Group highlights that this makes it particularly relevant for UCITS management companies authorised under Chapter 15 of the Law of 17 December 2010 and AIFMs authorised under Chapter 2 of the Law of 12 July 2013.

It has been revealed that there is some ambiguity over whether participation is optional. The CSSF communiqué states the questionnaire “must be completed and submitted” by the deadline, while the user guide calls participation voluntary but “strongly recommends” it. Zeidler Group advises managers to treat it as an expected submission, not least because a non-response will be visible to the supervisor.

The questionnaire has five sections: General, Digital Strategy, AI technologies, AI third-party providers, and up to ten AI use cases. The pivotal point is question 6, where firms classify their most advanced AI use case as concrete (A), experimental or proof of concept (B), or not planned within 12 months (C). Only option C restricts the exercise to the first two sections.

Recent findings suggest that zeidler Group warns that AI is often more widespread than firms assume. Staff using GenAI tools such as ChatGPT or Copilot may already fall under options A or B, and AI deployed by delegated portfolio managers, central administrators or other service providers may also be relevant, both for the survey and for delegate oversight.

Industry observers note that firms should check their eDesk dashboard, align answers with their DORA register of information, outsourcing and delegation records and internal AI policies, and be ready to explain material changes since 2024. Conducting officers, IT, compliance and risk teams should agree responses before submission.

Zeidler Group also recommends using the exercise as a gap analysis, particularly around AI policies, rules on public GenAI tools and staff AI literacy, which has been required for deployers under Article 4 of the EU AI Act since 2 February 2025.

For more, read the full report here.

Sources indicate that amazon Neptune Serverless now delivers up to 30% better performance at the same price per Neptune Capacity Unit, running on AWS Graviton4 processors. The upcoming Graviton4-based platform also brings an improved scaling algorithm that adjusts Neptune Capacity Units (NCUs) more closely to your workload. This especially helps applications with many concurrent graph queries, such as real-time fraud detection, recommendation engines and generative AI applications that run graph lookups on every request. Neptune Serverless scales database capacity automatically as your application’s demand changes, so you can run graph applications with spiky or unpredictable traffic, such as fraud detection, recommendation engines, and generative AI applications, without provisioning for peak capacity. You pay only for the capacity you use. All newly created Neptune Serverless instances will be using AWS Graviton4 processors. You can create new Neptune Serverless instances using AWS Management Console or the AWS CLI. You can upgrade existing clusters to the latest version in the next release. For more information on pricing and regional availability, refer to the Amazon Neptune pricing page and Neptune Serverless documentation.
